Could this be a normal struct (with named args)?  We don't really use this as a tuple in this code?
Done
Wouldn't have expected reference_wrapper to be needed here... must be something weird with a copy?

You cannot have a std::optional<Foo&>, so you have to use a reference_wrapper.  The `getRegistryFromPrefix` function returns an optional<RegistryEntry&> (ideally) so that's where the reference_wrapper comes from.

https://godbolt.org/z/31e5xWsds
ACK.
If we're doing this in the constructor before main(), how do we select which registries exist for this specific config?
I think this is a problem with the next commit.  We should discuss it there.  As is, this code has no change if the header file isn't used.
ACK
does static do anything if we're in a header here?
These are static members of a struct, not static variables in the namespace.  So yes, they are required to be static.
ACK
Presumably this code below needs to be maintained if the logging option isn't set to dbus?
I'm not sure what dbus has to do with this.  These are the existing registries.
If the logging option isn't set to dbus, we shouldn't be exposing registries that only exist on phosphor-logging, right?

> If the logging option isn't set to dbus, we shouldn't be exposing registries that only exist on phosphor-logging, right?

No, this isn't true.  The design was requested (by you and Jason, I think) to support a new `OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID` journal entry.  This is implemented in phosphor-logging:

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-logging/blob/master/lib/lg2_commit.cpp#L122
Do we need this header anymore?

Yes, we still need this header.  Overall, this commit is keeping effectively the same behavior as we use to have.  Except that rather than the hand-written `getRegistryHeaderAndUrlFromPrefix` function the crux of it is implemented by the registration hook (which you left comments about later).  Whatever headers are used, those registries are added to the map, so those registries are exported.
ACK
nit, put this on its own line please.
Done

Do we need a registration function if these are all static?  Just generate a file with the correct std::array in it?

This might be fine, I just don't understand why we have the complexity.

> Do we need a registration function if these are all static? Just generate a file with the correct std::array in it?

I'm not really getting what you mean by this.

In the next commit, I generate the full list of used registries (from the Redfish base registries) in `redfish-core/include/registries_selector.hpp`.  I guess rather than just generating an "include the header file" I could also generate a "here are the list of registries used".  That doesn't really seem much different one way or the other.

Later on when I add support for the dbus-generated registries, I then have to generate two different lists (with some kind of flag in this script to determine the name) and anyhow have some kind of "registration" code that loads the two lists into a combined list.

This hook function, to me, looks like less custom code because they're at least all done the same way.  It's just a one-line call here.

```
template <typename T>
void registerRegistry()
{
    allRegistries().emplace(T::header.registryPrefix,
                            RegistryEntry{T::header, T::url, T::registry});
}
```

my only thinking is that generating a file with the registries is clearer to debug, but I'm not going to hold up on ceremony/my opinions.

Fine as is.
I still don't like that we're doing something subtle here, and running code before main(), but it's not a reason to hold this up.
